evidence.passage: Asked on Diary of a CEO what he had meant, he said, "I was chasing being great," and that he would otherwise "perceive myself as a failure."
evidence.reason: Everything I could reopen was accurate and faithful to context. I found no misquotation among ~90 DOAC quotations checked against the publisher VTT (six checked by ear with Whisper) or among the GQ, Rolling Stone, Complex 2021, Billboard, The Nation, The Conversation, Daily Beast, UnHerd and X quotations. Prompts, auto-caption limits and transcript disagreements are disclosed at the relevant passage (e.g., only the words shared across transcripts before "perceive" are quoted). Self-report is kept separate from inference. The load-bearing rank evidence spans independent sources years apart. Provisional: about 30 used sources could not be opened or read this session (YouTube block, Essence 403, the Harlow render, TIME/Forbes/Wiki unread), so the Mafiathon, CBS, Essence and Harlow legs rest on the prior stages' checks, not mine.

enneagram.passage: So the call rests mainly on what he says he is chasing. A Seven chases options and avoids limits; Druski ranks himself against others and names failure as the outcome he refused to accept.
enneagram.reason: The motive is tied to repeated, costly choices: no plan B, no vacations, turning down paid cameos "thinking about my image", refusing to re-pitch while wanting the gatekeepers to "see what I was capable of doing". The Eight is argued at full strength ("If the evidence stopped here, Eight would be a fair call"), and a Seven test is added. The discriminator uses his own volunteered stake, and the criticism leg is honestly marked contested. The whiteface escalation and the self-roast are conceded as unexplained. Kept from a 9: the decisive rank evidence is self-report, and "number one" ambition is only moderately distinct from an Eight's drive to dominate.

originality.passage: Filming sketches around his mother's house, he gave her follower counts. Had he made any money? "No but I have people watching."
originality.reason: The details are specific to this person and verified: the private classroom poll ("why is Mikey funnier than me?"), follower counts reported to his mother, the Ricky Bobby family motto, the Joe Jackson belt line ("I've seen it before"), and the Michael Jackson persona answer. There is little reusable type boilerplate; the Type 3 definition is immediately converted into a person-specific test. The unresolved whiteface escalation survives the thesis.

writing.passage: The sketches are the Eight's strongest evidence: a large public risk, repeated, revived after the backlash and never taken back. "AM I CANCELLED?" and the "too far" post are taunts, which fit an Eight. The defense is where the Eight reading weakens.

The closing callback and five-year quote end on the story, not a moral. The drag is density: the whiteface and apologies sections stack three or four qualifying sentences per claim ("Legal caution explains some of the quiet. Billboard's acid test names the other half..."), and at 4,410 words the body is near the ceiling. Some Eight/Three weighing recurs across the type answer, self-funding, whiteface and apologies sections.
